newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S ZHIVKOV DENIES HOLDING MONEY IN SWISS BANKS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S ZHIVKOV DENIES HOLDING MONEY IN SWISS BANKS.

text.p: Bulgaria's former communist dictator Todor Zhivkov, eastern Europe's longest serving leader until his removal in a bloodless coup in 1989, has denied a Reuters report suggesting he held money in Swiss banks.
"Only Todor Zhivkov, of all other heads of state, has never held accounts in banks neither in this country nor abroad," Tuesday's Troud daily quoted Zhivkov as saying.
"This primitive insinuation is offensive and distressing."
A Reuters story from Zurich on May 16 saying Zhivkov "was rumoured to have money in Switzerland" was picked up by local newspapers.
Zhivkov was convicted in 1992 of embezzling 21.5 million levs (then about $24 million) of public funds, spent on luxury apartments and Western cars for his family and favoured aides.
Bulgarian prosecution officials in the past several years have tried to establish to no avail whether Zhivkov held accounts in banks abroad, said Troud.
In January the Sofia prosecutor freed Zhivkov in connection with embezzlement charges, but he remains under house arrest on separate charges.
Zhivkov now lives in his granddaughter's villa in Sofia's wealthy Boyana suburb and needs permission to leave it.
